mainTopic: רב's wording about רבי שמעון, and the פסוקים behind the limits on redeemed פסולי המוקדשין
overview: The גמרא first asks why רב said the משנה is the view of רבי שמעון alone, when the רבנן seem to agree with part of it. One answer is that רב follows ריש לקיש, so the burial rule for dead קדשי מזבח fits only רבי שמעון. Another answer is that רב follows רבי יוחנן, and we read his words as 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.' Next, a ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'like the צבי and the איל' that פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה and מתנות. The word אך keeps their חלב forbidden. רב פפא and אביי debate whether אך also keeps אותו ואת בנו in force. רבא instead learns the חלב law from 'דמו', which teaches that the fat carries full כרת, and he uses אך for אותו ואת בנו. Finally, a ברייתא shows that redeemed blemished קדשים may not be shorn, milked, or redeemed to feed dogs.

steps.title: רב should have mentioned רבי שמעון's disputants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב should have said 'This is רבי שמעון and his disputants,' not just 'רבי שמעון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have said: 'This is the opinion of רבי שמעון and of those who argue with him!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רב worded his statement about the משנה. Since the רבנן agree with part of the ruling, רב should have named them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי שמעון and the רבנן agree that an animal with a blemish before it was made holy can be redeemed. So it seems wrong to say the whole משנה is only רבי שמעון's view. The גמרא wants to know why רב left the רבנן out.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who argue with him (literally, 'his dispute')
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new question. It continues the earlier discussion of רב's statement that the משנה follows רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: 'This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him'
phrases.notes: This is the wording the גמרא thinks רב should have used; 'those who disagree with him' are the רבנן.

phrases.english: he should have said!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by challenging רב's earlier statement from the previous section
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that the משנה follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן agree with part of the ruling, so the wording 'רבי שמעון' alone is incomplete.

steps.title: רב follows ריש לקיש, so the משנה cannot fit the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב holds like ריש לקיש: for the רבנן, קדשי מזבח need no העמדה והערכה. So the clause 'if they died they must be buried' fits only רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: רב holds like רבי שמעון בן לקיש. He said that according to the רבנן, animals given to בדק הבית needed העמדה והערכה, but קדשי מזבח did not. So the משנה cannot be explained like the רבנן, because the last clause teaches: 'If they died, they must be buried.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב named only רבי שמעון. Under ריש לקיש's view, part of the משנה does not work for the רבנן at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead animal cannot be stood before a כהן and valued. So the rule that it must be buried shows it needs העמדה והערכה. According to ריש לקיש, the רבנן say קדשי מזבח do not need this. That means the burial rule matches only רבי שמעון, so רב was right to name him alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing the animal before a כהן and having him set its value, which is needed before redeeming it
Things made holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Animals made holy to be brought on the מזבח
Can be explained / set up as following
The last clause of a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one אמורא's position, here ריש לקיש's, can explain the exact wording another אמורא used.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: רַב כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ,
phrases.english: They said: Rav holds like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש, not the תנא רבי שמעון whose opinion the משנה follows.

phrases.english: who said: according to the Rabbis,
animals consecrated for Temple maintenance
were included in standing and valuation,
animals consecrated for the altar
were not included in standing and valuation,
and the Mishnah cannot be explained according to the Rabbis,
since the last clause teaches:
and if they died, they must be buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: רַב כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about רב's wording
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties רב to a specific אמורא's view of the רבנן, which makes the משנה fit only רבי שמעון
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן agree with the משנה, so רב should have named them
steps.terutzMaskana: Under ריש לקיש, the burial clause matches only רבי שמעון, so naming him alone is correct

steps.title: Maybe the burial is because we don't redeem holy animals for dog food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the burial rule comes from העמדה והערכה. Maybe it is because we do not redeem holy animals just to feed them to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone said: How do we know that 'if they died, they must be buried' is because they need העמדה והערכה? Maybe it is because we do not redeem holy animals in order to feed them to dogs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from the last step. It offers another reason why a dead holy animal must be buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If burial is only because of the rule against redeeming holy animals to feed dogs, then even the רבנן could agree with it. In that case the burial clause no longer proves the משנה follows רבי שמעון alone.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Maybe

keyTerms.term: אֵין פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים
keyTerms.meaning: We do not redeem holy animals in order to feed them to dogs

phrases.english: He said: From where do we know that this 'if they died they must be buried'
is because they require standing and valuation?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים
phrases.english: Perhaps it is because one may not redeem consecrated animals
in order to feed them to dogs!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהָא מֵתוּ יִקָּבֵרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning used in the answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the burial clause depends on העמדה והערכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another reason, not feeding dogs, could explain the burial, so the clause proves nothing about העמדה והערכה

steps.title: Then the משנה should have taught the case of a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: If the reason were only 'no redeeming for dogs,' the משנה would have taught that a טריפה must be buried. Since it says 'died,' the reason must be העמדה והערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: If so, let the משנה teach: 'If they became טריפה, they must be buried.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the alternative reason and defends the proof from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is still alive, so it can be stood and valued. Its flesh is forbidden, so it would only be redeemed for dogs. If that were the reason for burial, the משנה should have used the טריפה case. Since it chose 'died,' the burial must come from the need for העמדה והערכה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let it teach
An animal with a fatal injury, which may not be eaten

phrases.english: They said: If so, let it teach:
'If they became tereifa, they must be buried.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן נִיתְנֵי אִם נַעֲשׂוּ טְרֵיפָה יִקָּבֵרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge and keeps the first answer in place
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from the משנה's choice of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burial might come from the rule against redeeming for dogs
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's choice of 'died' shows burial comes from the need for העמדה והערכה

steps.title: רב follows רבי יוחנן, and his wording is changed
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רב really holds like רבי יוחנן, so the משנה can fit the רבנן. We change רב's words to 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: Really, רב holds like רבי יוחנן, and read his statement as: 'This is the opinion of רבי שמעון and those who argue with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question in step 1. It accepts the question and changes רב's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that for the רבנן, קדשי מזבח also need העמדה והערכה. Then the burial clause fits the רבנן too. So רב must have meant both opinions, and his wording is adjusted to match.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Really / in truth
He holds

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to explain רב: (1) He follows ריש לקיש, so the משנה is רבי שמעון alone, proven from 'if they died they must be buried.' (2) He follows רבי יוחנן, and his words are changed to 'רבי שמעון and his disputants.'

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם רַב כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: actually, Rav holds like Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנִי: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: and read: This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon and those who disagree with him.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting רב's words here, so read them the way step 1 suggested.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא לְעוֹלָם רַב כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, separate answer to the question in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of רב's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's wording 'רבי שמעון' alone must be explained
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יוחנן, and his statement should read 'רבי שמעון and his disputants'

steps.title: Asking for the source of the exemption when הקדש came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case (הקדש before the blemish) and asks where this exemption comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But if their הקדש came first, etc.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that if an animal was made holy and only later got a blemish, it is exempt from בכורה and מתנות even after it is redeemed. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Their being made holy came first, before the blemish
From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)
Etc.; the rest of the quoted line is understood

phrases.english: But if their consecration came first, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It leaves the earlier discussion about רב and העמדה והערכה and moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that פסולי המוקדשין whose הקדש came before the blemish are exempt from בכורה and מתנות.

steps.title: The word צבי teaches exemption from בכורה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word 'צבי' in the פסוק that פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה, just like a צבי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'צבי'. Just as a צבי is exempt from בכורה, so too פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The פסוק compares eating blemished holy animals to eating a צבי, and a צבי has no בכורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (דברים יב:כב) says blemished holy animals are eaten 'like the צבי and the איל'. The ברייתא reads the comparison as more than a rule about eating. Since a צבי, a wild animal, is not subject to בכורה, פסולי המוקדשין are not subject to it either.

keyTerms.meaning: Gazelle, a wild animal that has no בכורה law
Holy animals that got a blemish and were redeemed
The law of a firstborn male animal being given to the כהן

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"Gazelle":
phrases.notes: From the פסוק about blemished holy animals: 'just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so you shall eat it' (דברים יב:כב).

phrases.english: just as a gazelle is exempt from the firstborn law,
so too disqualified consecrated animals
are exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word צבי in the פסוק compares פסולי המוקדשין to a gazelle, which is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: Maybe they are exempt only from בכורה, not from מתנות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a doubt: the צבי comparison may teach only an exemption from בכורה, while the animals would still owe מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should I exclude them from בכורה but not exclude them from מתנות?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a follow-up: does the צבי comparison go far enough to exempt these animals from the מתנות too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempted these animals from both בכורה and מתנות. So far the ברייתא has a source only for בכורה, so it asks whether the מתנות still apply.

keyTerms.meaning: The gifts: the foreleg, cheeks and stomach given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal
I will exclude

phrases.english: Should I exclude them from the firstborn law,
but not exclude them from the gifts?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא אֲנִי אֶת הַבְּכוֹרָה וְלֹא אוֹצִיא אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the derivation in step 7 reaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צבי comparison was applied only to בכורה. Nothing yet exempts these animals from מתנות, which the משנה also exempted.

steps.title: The extra word איל adds the exemption from מתנות
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק also says 'איל', which teaches that פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from both בכורה and מתנות, like an איל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'איל': just as an איל is exempt from בכורה and from מתנות, so too פסולי המוקדשין are exempt from בכורה and from מתנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the second animal in the פסוק, the איל. That word adds the exemption from מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names two wild animals, צבי and איל. The ברייתא uses the second word to widen the comparison so it covers the מתנות as well as בכורה. Now the משנה's full ruling has a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Deer (hart), the second wild animal named in the פסוק
The פסוק teaches us (introduces a proof from a word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: The verse states: "hart":
phrases.notes: Here אַיָּל means a deer, not a ram. It is the second animal in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: just as a hart is exempt
from the firstborn law and from the gifts,
so too disqualified consecrated animals are exempt
from the firstborn law and from the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אַיָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional word in the פסוק widens the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the בכורה exemption is learned from צבי, so these animals would still owe מתנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The added word איל teaches an exemption from both בכורה and מתנות.

steps.title: Should their חלב also be permitted, like a צבי's?
steps.stepSummary: If פסולי המוקדשין are compared to צבי and איל, maybe their חלב should be permitted too, since the חלב of wild animals is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as the חלב of a צבי and an איל is permitted, should the חלב of פסולי המוקדשין also be permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes the comparison further to test it: does it also permit these animals' forbidden fat?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלב of wild animals is permitted. If the comparison to צבי and איל is complete, the חלב of blemished holy animals would be permitted too. That cannot be right, because they are domestic animals whose חלב is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Their forbidden fat (חלב)
Permitted
If so, then just as... (pushes a comparison further)

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל חֶלְבָּן מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: If so, just as the fat of a gazelle and a hart is permitted,
should the fat of disqualified consecrated animals also be permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל חֶלְבָּן מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of step 9 for going too far.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full comparison of פסולי המוקדשין to צבי and איל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, it should also permit their חלב, which is plainly wrong.

steps.title: The word אך limits the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אך' in the פסוק divides the cases, so the comparison does not extend to חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'אך'. It divides.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the word אך (however) at the start of the פסוק puts a limit on the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אך is a limiting word. It tells us the comparison to צבי and איל covers some laws (בכורה and מתנות) but not all of them. So the חלב of פסולי המוקדשין stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: However; a word in the פסוק that limits
It divided; it sets the cases apart

steps.whatToRemember: From the פסוק 'אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי ואת האיל': צבי teaches no בכורה, איל adds no מתנות, and אך keeps their חלב forbidden.

phrases.english: The verse states: "However"; it divides.
phrases.notes: The פסוק opens with אַךְ, 'however'. The word sets a limit, so the comparison to wild animals does not cover their fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר אַךְ חִלֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and completes the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to wild animals would also permit their חלב.
steps.terutzMaskana: אך limits the comparison, so it applies to בכורה and מתנות but not to חלב.

steps.title: Why would we first exempt only from בכורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line about exempting from בכורה but not מתנות, and asks what makes בכורה different.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'I will exclude them from בכורה but not exclude them from מתנות.' What is different, that I exclude from בכורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back and looks closely at one line of the ברייתא. It asks why we would have thought the צבי comparison exempts from בכורה but not from מתנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both בכורה and מתנות are gifts to the כהן, so it is not clear why the first word, צבי, should cover only one of them. The גמרא wants the reason behind the ברייתא's first assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here means the ברייתא we just learned. The גמרא is going back to quote it.

phrases.english: I will exclude them from the firstborn,
but I will not exclude them from the gifts.
What is different, that I would exclude only the firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר אוֹצִיא אֶת הַבְּכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the doubt raised in step 8 and asks for the reasoning behind it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא first assumed the צבי comparison exempts from בכורה but not from מתנות.

steps.title: בכורה applies only to males, while מתנות apply to all
steps.stepSummary: בכורה does not apply equally to all animals, so it is easier to exempt from. מתנות apply to all animals, so a separate word, איל, was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because בכורה does not apply equally to all animals. I would not exclude them from מתנות, because the מתנות apply equally to all. So the פסוק says 'איל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that בכורה is a narrow law, while מתנות are a wide law, and that is why the ברייתא needed the extra word איל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בכורה applies only to a firstborn male, so it is a limited law and easy to exempt from with one word. מתנות apply to every slaughtered domestic animal, male or female, so it takes more to exempt from them. That is why a second word, איל, was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Applies equally to all animals
Because it does not

steps.whatToRemember: A narrow law (בכורה, only firstborn males) can be removed with one word, צבי. A broad law (מתנות, all animals) needed the extra word איל.

phrases.english: Because it does not apply equally to all,
phrases.notes: בכורה applies only to a firstborn male, not to females or to animals born later.

phrases.english: and I would not exclude them from the gifts
because they apply equally to all.
phrases.notes: The gifts are taken from every domestic animal that is slaughtered, male or female.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "hart."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בכורה is limited to firstborn males, so it is easier to exempt from. מתנות apply to all animals, so a separate word, איל, was needed to exempt from them.

steps.title: רב פפא: Maybe the comparison also cancels 'it and its offspring'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that if פסולי המוקדשין are compared to צבי and איל, they should be exempt from אותו ואת בנו, just like those wild animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If you compare them to a צבי and an איל, then just as אותו ואת בנו does not apply to those animals, it should also not apply to פסולי המוקדשין!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a new challenge from the same comparison to צבי and איל. This time he asks about the law of not slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In earlier steps, the comparison to צבי and איל freed פסולי המוקדשין from בכורה and מתנות, and the word אך stopped it from reaching חלב. רב פפא now asks why the comparison does not also free them from אותו ואת בנו, which does not apply to wild animals. Nothing in the ברייתא seems to block this.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against slaughtering an animal and its young on the same day
Applies; is in force
If just as ... so too: pushing a comparison to its full result

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
If so, just as a gazelle and a hart,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ נוֹהֵג בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: the law of 'it and its offspring' does not apply to them,
so too, disqualified consecrated animals,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ נוֹהֵג בּוֹ!
phrases.english: 'it and its offspring' should not apply to them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: אִי מָה צְבִי וְאַיָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the comparison challenge from step 10, this time to אותו ואת בנו instead of חלב
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of פסולי המוקדשין to צבי and איל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison works, it should carry over every leniency of wild animals, including the exemption from אותו ואת בנו, and the ברייתא never addresses this.

steps.title: אביי: Every domesticated animal is bound by 'it and its offspring'
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that whether you treat them like חולין or like קדשים, domesticated animals are bound by אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What are you comparing them to? If to חולין animals, אותו ואת בנו applies. If to קדשים, אותו ואת בנו also applies!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא. He says the comparison to wild animals cannot exempt פסולי המוקדשין from אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסולי המוקדשין sit between two categories: ordinary animals and holy animals. Both of those categories are bound by אותו ואת בנו. So אביי says there is no category these animals could fit into where the law would not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: To what are you comparing them?
Ordinary, non-holy animals
Holy, sacrificial animals

phrases.english: He said to him: To what are you comparing them?
phrases.notes: Here אביי is answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: If to non-sacred animals,
'it and its offspring' applies to it,
and if to sacrificial animals,
'it and its offspring' applies to it as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמַאי מְדַמֵּית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical argument: every possible category already has the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to צבי and איל would free פסולי המוקדשין from אותו ואת בנו
steps.terutzMaskana: Since both חולין and קדשים are bound by אותו ואת בנו, the comparison cannot exempt them

steps.title: רב פפא: By that logic, 'אך' would not be needed for fat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects אביי's answer. The same reasoning would make the word אך pointless for חלב, since חלב is forbidden in both חולין and קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: If so, we could say the same thing about חלב. What are you comparing them to? If to חולין, their חלב is forbidden. If to קדשים, their חלב is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא shows that אביי's answer proves too much. If it were correct, the ברייתא would not have needed the word אך to keep חלב forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, the ברייתא used the word אך to stop the comparison from permitting חלב. But חלב is forbidden in both ordinary and holy domesticated animals, the same pattern as אותו ואת בנו. If אביי's logic worked, the ברייתא would never have needed אך, so his logic cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is right
Forbidden fat of a domesticated animal
Let us say the same thing

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: Now רב פפא is speaking again.

phrases.english: regarding its fat as well, let us say the same:
To what are you comparing them?
If to non-sacred animals, their fat is forbidden,
and if to sacrificial animals, their fat is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי חֶלְבּוֹ נָמֵי נֵימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 15 by applying it to חלב
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's argument that the comparison cannot exempt them because both categories are bound
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the word אך unnecessary for חלב, yet the ברייתא clearly needed אך for that

steps.title: The word 'אך' blocks both fat and 'it and its offspring'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives the real answer. Just as אך keeps חלב forbidden, it also keeps אותו ואת בנו in force for פסולי המוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, didn't you say that אך teaches 'but not their חלב'? Say also that אך teaches 'but not אותו ואת בנו.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his point and offers the true solution. The same word אך that limited the comparison for חלב also limits it for אותו ואת בנו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason פסולי המוקדשין are still bound by אותו ואת בנו is not logic about categories. It is the word אך in the פסוק, which cuts the comparison off. So the comparison to צבי and איל gives only the exemptions from בכורה and מתנות, and nothing more.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; introduces the correct approach
Didn't you say?
'However': a limiting word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison of פסולי המוקדשין to צבי and איל exempts them only from בכורה and מתנות. The word אך keeps both חלב and אותו ואת בנו in force for them.

phrases.english: Rather, didn't you say
'However', but not their fat?
Say also: 'However'
but not 'it and its offspring.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָאו מִי אָמְרַתְּ ״אַךְ״ וְלֹא חֶלְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with the correct source: the word אך
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source reading: the limiting word אך
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison would free them from אותו ואת בנו, or only category logic keeps the law in force
steps.terutzMaskana: The word אך limits the comparison, so פסולי המוקדשין remain bound by אותו ואת בנו just as their חלב stays forbidden

steps.title: רבא splits the two sources: אך for אותו ואת בנו, דמו for fat
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the word אך is needed only for אותו ואת בנו. The prohibition of חלב in פסולי המוקדשין comes from a different word, "דמו".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: The word "אך" comes to teach about אותו ואת בנו. The fat prohibition comes from the word "דמו", as it says: "Only its blood you shall not eat."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to answer רב פפא's problem. He assigns אך to אותו ואת בנו only and finds a separate source for חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא used one word, אך, to cover both חלב and אותו ואת בנו. רבא divides the job: אך keeps אותו ואת בנו in force, and the פסוק about the firstborn, "רק את דמו לא תאכל", is the source for חלב. The next steps explain how "blood" can mean fat.

keyTerms.meaning: "However / only": a limiting word that excludes something from the comparison to צבי ואיל
The ban on slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day
"It comes out": it is learned or derived from
"Only": another limiting word, here in the פסוק about a blemished בכור

phrases.english: Rava says:
"However" comes only for the law of a mother and its offspring,
and its fat is derived from "its blood,"
as it is written: "Only you shall not eat its blood."
phrases.notes: This פסוק is about a firstborn animal with a blemish, which is eaten "like the צבי and the איל".

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: ״אַךְ״ לְאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב פפא's in step 17. It splits the sources instead of using אך for both laws.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning sources: each law gets its own word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a single אך must cover both חלב and אותו ואת בנו.
steps.terutzMaskana: אך covers אותו ואת בנו. The prohibition of חלב comes from "דמו".

steps.title: What does 'its blood' mean? It cannot be real blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what "דמו" refers to. It rules out actual blood, since the blood of צבי and איל is forbidden anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "its blood"? If you say it means actual blood, that makes no sense. Even if this animal were treated just like a צבי or איל, is the blood of a צבי or איל permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רבא's reading. It shows that "דמו" cannot mean ordinary blood, which prepares the way for the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is forbidden in every animal, wild or domesticated. So even if the blemished בכור is compared fully to צבי ואיל, its blood is already forbidden. A פסוק that only said "don't eat its blood" would teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you say": opens a possible reading that is about to be rejected
Actual, literal
"Is that to say...?": introduces a question whose answer is obviously no
Permitted

phrases.english: What is "its blood"?
If we say it means its actual blood,

phrases.aramaic: לָא יְהֵא אֶלָּא דָּמָן דִּצְבִי וְאַיָּל,
phrases.english: let it be no more than the blood of a gazelle and a hart,

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ דָּמָן דִּצְבִי וְאַיָּל מִי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: is the blood of a gazelle and a hart permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״דָּמוֹ״? אִילֵּימָא דָּמוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the word "דמו" that רבא used as his source in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word "דמו" in the פסוק actually refers to, since plain blood would be pointless to mention.

steps.title: 'Its blood' means its fat
steps.stepSummary: Since real blood is already forbidden, the גמרא concludes that "דמו" here means חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, "its blood" means its fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: in this פסוק, "blood" stands for fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The literal meaning would add nothing, so the word is read as teaching something new. That new thing is that the fat of the blemished בכור stays forbidden, even though the animal is otherwise compared to צבי ואיל, whose fat is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of a domesticated animal; the fat of wild animals like צבי and איל is permitted
"Rather": introduces the correct reading after rejecting the first one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תורה permits the blood of this animal. Its blood is forbidden like all blood. The word "דמו" is simply being used to teach about its fat.

phrases.english: Rather, "its blood" means its fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 by reading "דמו" as חלב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "דמו" refers to the animal's fat, teaching that its חלב remains forbidden.

steps.title: Then why not just write 'its fat'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if fat is meant, the תורה should have written "חלבו" directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the תורה write "its fat"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading it just gave. If the point is fat, why would the תורה use the word "blood"?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading "blood" as "fat" is a stretch. The challenge demands a reason why the plain word "חלב" would not have done the job.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let it write": the Torah should have written
"The Merciful One": a name for God / the תורה as author of the פסוק

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write "its fat"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״חֶלְבּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 20 based on the תורה's choice of words.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורה meant fat, the direct word "חלבו" was available, so choosing "דמו" needs explaining.

steps.title: Writing 'fat' would have suggested a split ruling
steps.stepSummary: Had the תורה written "חלב", we would have thought the היקש to צבי ואיל and the פסוק each have some effect. The result would be only a partial prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the תורה had written "fat", I would have said: the comparison has an effect, and the פסוק has an effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It explains the wrong conclusion we would have drawn if the word "חלב" had been written, and the next step spells out the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two forces pull in opposite directions. The היקש to צבי ואיל points toward permitting the fat, and a פסוק saying "חלב" points toward forbidding it. With both in play, we would have given each one partial power, so the fat would be forbidden, but not with the full severity.

keyTerms.meaning: "I would have said": the mistaken assumption one might have
"It is effective": it has some effect
The היקש: a comparison the תורה makes by placing two things together, here to צבי and איל
The פסוק, the verse

phrases.english: If the Merciful One had written "fat,"
I would have said:
the comparison is effective and the verse is effective.
phrases.notes: He means each source would get partial power, so the fat would end up forbidden, but only partly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״חֵלֶב״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the plain word would have led to a mistaken compromise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With "חלב" written, the היקש and the פסוק would share the effect, giving only a partial prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the תורה avoided the plain word "חלב" and wrote "דמו" instead. Steps 23-25 spell out both halves of the mistaken compromise and why "דמו" avoids it.

steps.title: The comparison would have removed the כרת punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the היקש's share. It would have exempted this fat from כרת, because כרת is written only about the fat of a regular בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The comparison would be effective to exclude כרת. When the תורה writes כרת, it is written about one who eats the fat of a domesticated animal, as it says: "For anyone who eats the fat of the domesticated animal..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the first half of the mistaken compromise from step 22: what the היקש would have accomplished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת punishment in ויקרא is tied to "the fat of the בהמה". Since the היקש compares this animal to wild animals like צבי ואיל, we would have said it falls outside that פסוק, so there is no כרת. In this mistaken view, the היקש takes away the כרת while the פסוק still forbids the fat.

keyTerms.meaning: "To exclude": to remove something from a rule
Spiritual cutting off, the severe punishment for eating forbidden fat
A domesticated animal, as opposed to a wild animal (חיה) like צבי and איל

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא pays attention to exactly which category a punishment is attached to. Because the כרת פסוק says "בהמה", the comparison to wild animals could have been used to remove that punishment.

phrases.english: The comparison is effective to exclude from karet,
because when it writes karet,
it is written about one who eats the fat of a domesticated animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי כׇל אוֹכֵל חֵלֶב מִן הַבְּהֵמָה״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: "For anyone who eats the fat of the domesticated animal."
phrases.notes: That פסוק in ויקרא goes on to say the person is cut off. Since this animal is compared to wild ones, we might think it is not counted as a בהמה here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֲנִי הֶיקֵּישָׁא לְמַעוֹטֵי מִכָּרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the היקש part of the mistaken view described in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the details of the mistaken view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש to צבי ואיל would take this fat out of the כרת פסוק, which speaks only of "בהמה".
steps.terutzMaskana: This explains part of why writing "חלב" would have been misleading.

steps.title: The verse's share would have been only a plain prohibition
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written "חלבו", the פסוק's only contribution would have been a plain לאו on the fat, with no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the verse would also have done something: it would have made eating the fat a plain prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the "split result" idea from the last steps. The היקש would remove כרת, and the פסוק would still leave a plain לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the היקש's share was to exempt the fat from כרת. Here we learn the פסוק's share. It would still forbid the fat, but only as a לאו, which is punished with מלקות. So writing "חלבו" would have produced a weaker prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Had an effect; did something
The verse
A plain negative commandment, punished with lashes and not כרת

phrases.english: And the verse would have had an effect
to establish it as a mere prohibition,
phrases.notes: "It" means eating the fat of these disqualified קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַהֲנִי קְרָא לְמֵיקַם עֲלֵיהּ בְּלָאו בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the split described in steps 22-23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the hypothetical outcome had the verse said "חלבו"
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With "חלבו", the fat would carry only a לאו
steps.terutzMaskana: This explains why the תורה avoided the word "חלבו"

steps.title: The תורה wrote "its blood" to teach כרת for the fat
steps.stepSummary: Therefore the תורה used the word "דמו". Just as blood carries כרת, so does this fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the תורה said "its blood": to teach that just as eating its blood brings כרת, eating its fat also brings כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes why the word "דמו" was chosen. It links the fat to blood, so the fat gets the full punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the fat "blood" ties the two together, so the fat gets blood's punishment, כרת. This shows that for this law the היקש to צבי ואיל does not apply at all. That answers the question from step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Expressed it using the wording of
Spiritual cutting-off, the severe punishment for eating blood or forbidden fat

steps.whatToRemember: "דמו" in this פסוק means the fat. The fat of disqualified קדשים carries כרת just like blood, and the היקש to צבי ואיל does not lighten this.

phrases.english: For this reason the Merciful One expressed it
in the language of "its blood," to tell you:
just as its blood is punished with כרת
so too its fat is punished with כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהָכִי אַפְּקֵיהּ רַחֲמָנָא בִּלְשׁוֹן דָּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the hypothetical in steps 22-24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The word "דמו" teaches that the fat of disqualified קדשים carries full כרת

steps.title: But the ברייתא learned the fat law from "however"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the ברייתא used the word "אך" to show the fat is not covered by the היקש. So why use "דמו"?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא of the ברייתא said that "אך" teaches the היקש does not cover its fat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that "דמו" is the source. It points out that the ברייתא already used a different word, "אך", for this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said "אך" limits the היקש to צבי ואיל: it removes בכורה and gifts, but not the fat prohibition. If "אך" already handles the fat, then "דמו" seems unnecessary as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the תנא teach...
"Only/however," a word in the פסוק that limits a law

phrases.english: But didn't the tanna
say "however," but not its fat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תָּנָא אַךְ וְלֹא חֶלְבּוֹ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source identified in step 25 using the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "דמו" is the source for the fat's prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already learned the fat law from "אך", so "דמו" would be extra

steps.title: Once "its blood" is written, "however" teaches אותו ואת בנו
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only meant that "אך" would teach the fat law if "דמו" were missing. Since "דמו" is written, "אך" teaches אותו ואת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: had "its blood" not been written, I would have used "אך" to teach the fat law. Now that "its blood" is written, "אך" teaches that אותו ואת בנו applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It reads the ברייתא as a "what if", so "אך" is freed up for a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since "דמו" already covers the fat, "אך" is not needed for that. Instead it teaches that the ban on slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day applies to disqualified קדשים. This way both words teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
The ban on slaughtering an animal and its offspring on the same day
Now that it is stated

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying "אך" is the actual source for the fat. That was only true if "דמו" were missing. In the end "אך" teaches אותו ואת בנו.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Had "its blood" not been stated,
I would have said "however" teaches: but not its fat;
now that "its blood" is stated,
it comes for the law of "it and its offspring."
phrases.notes: "It" is the word "אך". It now teaches that the mother-and-young ban applies to these animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר אִילּוּ לֹא נֶאֱמַר דָּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by reinterpreting the ברייתא

steps.title: Source for blemished קדשים not becoming fully non-sacred
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: redeemed קדשים whose הקדש came before the blemish do not become fully חולין. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And they do not go out to be fully non-sacred." From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that even after redemption, these animals may not be shorn or used for work. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches these limits.

steps.title: Slaughter but not shear, meat but not milk, eat but not feed dogs
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the words of the פסוק as limits. You may slaughter but not shear, eat the meat but not the milk, and eat it yourself but not feed it to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "You may slaughter", but not shear. "Meat", but not milk. "And you shall eat", but not to your dogs. From here we learn that we do not redeem קדשים in order to feed them to dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It reads each word of the פסוק about redeemed blemished קדשים as allowing one thing and excluding another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows only slaughtering and eating the meat. So shearing, milk and feeding dogs stay forbidden, which shows the animal never becomes fully חולין. The last line adds a practical rule: you may not redeem קדשים just to feed them to dogs.
